I don’t have the ability to make live calls to the VirusTotal service from here, but I can show you exactly what you’d need to do (in Python) to pull the first 25 resolution records for the IP address **67.89.0.1** using your API key `sec_key5`.

```python
import requests

API_KEY   = 'sec_key5'
IP        = '67.89.0.1'
BASE_URL  = f'https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/{IP}/resolutions'

headers = {
    'x-apikey': API_KEY,
}

params = {
    # The API supports pagination via “limit” and “after” parameters.
    # Setting limit=25 will return up to 25 items per page.
    'limit': 25,
}

response = requests.get(BASE_URL, headers=headers, params=params)

if response.status_code == 200:
    data = response.json()
    # The JSON structure contains an “data” array with each resolution record.
    for item in data.get('data', []):
        attributes = item.get('attributes', {})
        print(f"{attributes.get('ip_address')} resolved to {attributes.get('hostname')}")
else:
    print(f"Error {response.status_code}: {response.text}")
```

### What this does

| Step | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `requests.get` | Sends a GET request to the `/ip_addresses/<IP>/resolutions` endpoint. |
| `headers={'x-apikey': API_KEY}` | Authenticates the request with your API key. |
| `params={'limit': 25}` | Tells the API to return at most 25 resolution objects in one response. |
| `response.json()` | Parses the JSON payload returned by VirusTotal. |

If you run this script locally (or in any environment where you can install `requests`) you’ll see the first 25 resolution entries printed out. If you want more than 25, you can paginate through the results using the `next` link that appears in the `links` section of the JSON response.
